name: Raindrop.io
tagline: Visual bookmark manager for saving, tagging, and searching links

pricing.notes: Official Pro URLs checked; public references list Pro at about $3/month depending on billing/currency.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Unlimited bookmarks, collections, highlights, devices and collaborators; 100 MB file uploads/month

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited bookmarks; 10 GB file uploads/month; full-text search, permanent archive, AI assistant, reminders and daily backups
tiers.notes: Official Raindrop blog states $3/month or $2.30/month on annual billing; VAT may be added.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Unlimited bookmarks, collections, highlights, devices and collaborators; 100 MB file uploads/month
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (yearly usually about 20% cheaper); Paddle billing; 30-day money-back guarantee
pricing.hiddenCosts: VAT may be added. Failed payments can be retried up to 4 times in the next week before downgrade to Free.

verdictSummary: A personal bookmark saver with tags, full-text search, and screenshots is a very tractable small app.
coreLoopDIY: Build a browser extension/bookmarklet, save URL metadata to SQLite/Postgres, tag it, optionally archive page text, and provide search.
requirements: small hosted backend or local database
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because bookmarks are boring until import/export, search, mobile, and extension reliability matter.

priorArt.name: linkwarden
priorArt.desc: Open-source bookmark manager with archiving, collections, and collaborative saving.

alternatives.name: Karakeep
alternatives.desc: A bookmark junk drawer that labels itself and keeps the contents.

facts.install: Official Docker Compose stack for the free self-hosted route, or a hosted Karakeep Cloud signup
facts.engines: Automatic tagging and OCR can use OpenAI or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, Azure OpenAI, or a local Ollama model; Tesseract is the default non-LLM OCR path.
facts.dataFormat: Bookmarks and metadata live in SQLite under the persistent data directory; page screenshots, PDFs, readable text, and uploads live on local or S3-compatible storage, with Meilisearch indexes in its own volume.
facts.gapVsPaid: Karakeep has weaker visual-collection design, native mobile polish, sharing, browser-extension refinement, and instant hosted convenience than Raindrop.io.
facts.setupBlocker: The free route needs Docker Compose, persistent secrets and volumes, a browser worker/Chrome, Meilisearch, HTTPS, backups, and optionally an API key or Ollama for AI features.

alternatives.name: LinkAce
alternatives.desc: A serious bookmark archive, right down to checking whether the links died.

facts.install: Official Docker Compose stack for self-hosting, or a paid managed/one-click host
facts.dataFormat: Links, lists, tags, notes, users, and status checks live in MariaDB/MySQL; the application, search, cache, and backup files live in persistent volumes, while archival references can point to the Internet Archive rather than a local page copy.
facts.gapVsPaid: LinkAce is a utilitarian web archive rather than Raindrop's polished visual organizer and has weaker native apps, previews, collaboration, and cross-device capture.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting starts with a multi-service stack, Docker, MariaDB, Meilisearch, Redis, scheduled jobs, HTTPS, backups, and upgrades.

alternatives.name: linkding
alternatives.desc: Pinboard with a nicer face and no annual invoice.

facts.install: Run the single official Docker container and create the first superuser
facts.dataFormat: Bookmarks, tags, notes, users, and metadata live in a persistent SQLite database by default or PostgreSQL; the optional plus image stores locally captured HTML snapshots and browser data in the mounted data directory.
facts.gapVsPaid: linkding is intentionally text-first and lacks Raindrop's visual collections, rich previews, polished native apps, sharing, collaboration, and hosted sync.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker and a persistent data volume are the first hurdle; reliable local page archiving requires the larger Chromium-equipped plus image rather than the standard lightweight image.

alternatives.name: Linkwarden
alternatives.desc: Raindrop with a filing cabinet and a copy of every page.

facts.install: Hosted signup or the official Docker Compose self-hosting stack
facts.engines: Automatic tagging can use Ollama, OpenAI or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, or Perplexity.
facts.dataFormat: Collections, links, tags, users, and annotations live in PostgreSQL; screenshots, PDFs, readable archives, previews, and uploads live on local persistent storage or configured S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Linkwarden is capable but its self-hosted route is less effortless and its visual organization, native-app ecosystem, browser polish, and consumer sharing trail Raindrop.io.
facts.setupBlocker: The indefinitely free route requires Docker, PostgreSQL, authentication secrets, persistent archive storage, a reverse proxy with HTTPS, backups, and upgrades.

notes: Great cheap-subscription target; a strong yes with real prior art.
prompt:
Build me a personal bookmark manager to replace Raindrop.io. Requirements:

- A local web app: Node + Express + better-sqlite3 on localhost:4040, server-rendered,
  minimal JS.
- Save via a bookmarklet that POSTs the current URL to /save; the server fetches the
  page, pulls title/description/og:image with metascraper, and stores the readable
  article text (@mozilla/readability) for search.
- Bookmarks take free-form tags (comma entry, autocomplete from existing tags) and an
  optional note.
- Full-text search across title, note, and archived page text with SQLite FTS5; filter
  by tag, newest first.
- List view: favicon, title, domain, tags, saved date. A weekly node-cron job re-checks
  links and flags 404s.
- Import from a Netscape bookmarks HTML export; export everything as JSON and CSV from
  an /export route.
- Binds to localhost only; no accounts, no telemetry, the whole archive is one SQLite
  file I can back up.
- Out of scope: mobile apps and full page-snapshot archiving, the stored text is the
  archive. No team collections.
- README: how to install the bookmarklet and where the DB file lives.
